A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CompreSSM work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LRU compression experiments, including accuracy, state dimensions, training times and HSV trajectories in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and reports additional compression comparisons, controlled ablations, pragmatic-variant results, timing measurements and Mamba experiments.

M1.justification: The original tolerance-based algorithm remains. New Section 3.2 adds fixed-fraction truncation with validation checks, checkpoint rollback and stopping after degradation. Appendix E.3 extends v1's mean-system suggestion into a Mamba procedure using calibration, cached per-channel transforms and rank-aware selective-scan execution.

E1.justification: The same MNIST/sMNIST, CIFAR10, ListOps, AAN, IMDB and Pathfinder tasks are used. MNIST becomes sMNIST without evidence of changed data or task requirements. Additional architectures, compression methods and timing studies do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares compressed LRUs with models trained directly at fixed dimensions. v3 actually evaluates HNN-regularized, subsequently truncated LRUs on sMNIST and knowledge distillation on CIFAR10 (Tables 2, 6 and 7). It also introduces random-HSV and top-HSV truncation controls; merely cited alternatives in v1 were not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The retained LRU benchmark settings remain unchanged. New protocols include controlled 256-to-32-state ablations varying reduction counts and windows, validation-based acceptance of pragmatic reductions, Mamba state-size sweeps, and operation-level timing benchmarks. Appendix F specifies full-size HNN training followed by truncation and teacher–student distillation experiments.

E4.justification: v1's HSV-trajectory analyses are retained as Figures 21–24. New Appendix C tests bottom versus random versus top HSV removal, reduction frequency and early versus late reduction windows. Appendices B, D and E additionally analyze pragmatic compression variability, computational bottlenecks and Mamba's weak size–performance relationship.

E5.justification: The main experiments retain five-seed, top-3/top-1 reporting. New ablations specify ten-seed averages, and Tables 6–7 state ten seeds without establishing that retained results were rerun. Figure 18 adds summaries excluding the best and worst runs, although its mean-versus-median labeling is inconsistent.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical results remain unchanged, but v3 adds comparator, pragmatic, Mamba, ablation and timing results. For example, Table 2 reports CIFAR10 accuracy of 79.4% for KD versus the retained 84.4% for CompreSSM at approximately 57 states. Table 4 also replaces v1 Table 3's MNIST zero entries with 12.7±3.0 states and 96.1%/93.3% compressed/baseline accuracies.

T1.justification: The central assumptions, truncation bound and HSV-continuity lemma remain. v3 corrects Equation 14's observability numerator from CC^T to C^T C and adds wall-clock accounting and reduction-complexity derivations in Appendix D. Appendix F adds an HNN objective and differentiability argument, although Equation 28 incorrectly identifies the sum of HSVs as the nuclear norm of PQ.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: principled early balanced truncation preserves useful SSM dynamics, improves training efficiency and extends to selective systems. The additional variant and experiments do not materially redefine the advertised core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 substantially extends v1's discussion of size–accuracy dependence, recovery time and selective-system caveats. It interprets truncation ablations, explains CPU/JIT overheads, proposes SISO structure as an explanation for weak Mamba size benefits, and discusses the pragmatic variant's tradeoff between simpler tuning and unpredictable final dimensions.

D1.justification: v1's hyperparameters and reduction schedules are retained. v3 newly provides a code repository address, RTX 6000 timing context, CPU/GPU placement and JIT overhead information, JAX/PyTorch implementation distinctions, Mamba transform/kernel details, and HNN stabilization and distillation hyperparameters. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused discussion of HSV regularization by Schwerdtner et al. (2025), initialization by Yu et al. (2024), and additional selective/linear-attention architectures and distillation references. It sharpens comparisons with existing compression approaches while retaining the original literature categories and first principled in-training MOR positioning.

P1.justification: Much main-text wording remains, but the appendices undergo substantial narrative reorganization. Implementation and results material is regrouped, the HSV-stability explanation is rewritten and expanded, and the brief selective-system outlook develops into detailed SISO/MIMO and Mamba explanations. Dedicated variant and comparator subsections also change the main-text organization.

P2.justification: v3 adds extensive ablation, timing and Mamba plots, architectural and distillation diagrams, and comparison/variant tables. Figure 3b changes from normalized training time to speedup. Original HSV Figures 5–8 are retained and relocated as Figures 21–24, rather than constituting new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly validates compression against fixed-size training and HSV trajectories. v3 addresses important validation gaps through controlled truncation/schedule ablations, evaluated compression alternatives, a Mamba implementation study, and substantially better timing and reproducibility documentation. New inconsistencies in norm notation, seed counts and timing labels limit confidence in some details, but the added evidence substantially strengthens understanding of why and when the method helps.
